generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, this means using the same habit on every essay and report, whatever the topic. Whether you cite a study, a theory or a textbook, you credit the idea, build the reference in APA, and check it is accurate. A reference to a journal article and one to a textbook go through the same habit. Making this your normal way of working is what keeps your psychology referencing trustworthy.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two psychology students each use several sources in an essay on a theory. Tom pastes in ready-made references at the end and references only his direct quotations, leaving his paraphrased studies unmarked. Amara uses the whole habit: crediting each study as she uses it, building each reference in APA from its parts, and checking them for accuracy. Both knew the studies, but Amara's referencing is trustworthy, because she used every strand together.
generatedProse.summary: Referencing in psychology is most useful when you treat it as one habit, not three separate ideas. On every essay and report you run the same strands together: know why you credit a source, know its parts, and set it out accurately in APA. Making this your normal way of working is what keeps your psychology referencing trustworthy.

check.body: A student uses an author's idea in an essay. They put it in their own words, add an in-text reference, build it from its parts in their department's style, and check it is accurate. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first report, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next report.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the student is using the whole referencing habit: knowing it is needed, building it from its parts, and setting it out accurately.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three strands are there, working together as one habit.

_items.text: That the student is doing more than referencing a source needs.
_items.feedback: No. Each part does a different job, and together they make the reference trustworthy.

_items.text: That only the in-text reference really matters.
_items.feedback: Not so. Crediting, the parts and accuracy all matter together.

_items.text: That paraphrasing does not need a reference.
_items.feedback: A paraphrase needs a reference just as a quotation does.
